answer.summary: Henrickson says Rippling prioritizes fast decisions: resolve them in the meeting, or bring in the needed person and finish that day. He qualifies that approach for irreversible decisions, which may need more careful handling; product and architecture choices that are hard to unwind can justify spending more time upfront.

sections.heading: Fast decisions are the norm
sections.content: Henrickson describes Rippling as valuing decision-making tempo and speed of response. Rather than schedule another meeting, teams should make the decision while together—or Slack-call whoever is needed—and have it decided that day.

sections.heading: Irreversible decisions are an exception
sections.content: He acknowledges that some irreversible decisions cannot be made on that same quick basis. In product design, he notes that assumptions built into a product can be extremely difficult to unwind later. For those choices, Rippling may spend more time ensuring the design can accommodate complex future needs, even if those needs are not supported in the first version.
